workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§265–266
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§265–266: The Tangut campaign and Chinggis’s rewards
part: §§265–266 — The Tangut campaign and Chinggis’s rewards
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§265–266, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Chinggis winters, then rides against the Tangut. Thrown from his horse by startled wild asses, he lies feverish while his princes urge a withdrawal; he sends an envoy to remind the Tangut ruler Burqan of his broken word. Asha Gambu takes the taunt on himself and challenges them to fight at Alashai, and Chinggis, saying “Eternal Heaven, you know it,” goes, defeats him and has his people plundered. Then, from Chasutu, he finishes the rebels, and gives Bo’orchu and Muqali the Jüin people of the Kitad as a reward. A note on the text: the Mongol is a Ming Chinese-character transcription, and the glosses in square brackets are the Ming glossators’ own; where the English departs from them or is unsure, the note says so.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Tere übül übülžežü Taṅγ̇ud irgen-dür morilaja keġen

morph.gloss: the Tangut, a people (people name; plural in -d) [種名]
people, the common folk (noun) [百姓 行]

sentences.l: That winter, wintering, Tangut people-to, let-us-ride saying,
sentences.i: That winter, as he wintered, he said, “Let us ride against the Tangut people,”
sentences.n: Tere übül übülžežü is “that winter, wintering”: übül “winter” + the verb-maker -že- + the converb -žü (Ming 住冬着). Morilaja is mori “horse” + -la- “to ride” + the hortative -ja, “let us mount” (Ming 上馬咱), and keġen “saying” closes the quotation. Irgen-dür is the dative-locative with the Ming 行, “against the Tangut people”. No opening quotation mark is printed; I supply it in `i`, and the speaker (Chinggis) is left unnamed in the Mongol.

sentences.t: šini toγ̇a toγ̇ulažu noγai žil namur Čiṅgis Qaγan Taṅγ̇ud irgen-dür morilaba.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 (name) [太祖︀]
the Tangut, a people (people name; plural in -d) [種名]
people, the common folk (noun) [百姓 行]

sentences.l: New count counting, Dog year, autumn, Chinggis Qaγan Tangut people-to mounted.
sentences.i: he took a new reckoning, and in the autumn of the Dog year Chinggis Qahan rode against the Tangut people.
sentences.n: Šini toγ̇a toγ̇ulažu is toγ̇a “number” + -la- + the converb -žu, “counting a new count” (Ming 新 數 數着). I take it as a fresh muster of his force, but that is a guess from the words alone. Noγai žil is “Dog year”, in the twelve-year animal cycle, here followed by namur “autumn”. Morilaba is mori + -la- + the past -ba, the same stem as in the last unit, now a fact, “rode”.

sentences.t: Qatun-dāča Jesüi Qatun-(n)i abču odba.

morph.gloss: lady, queen, wife of a khan (noun) [娘子 內]
ablative: from, among (back-vowel form; long vowel as printed)
Yesui, a woman's name (personal name) [(婦人)名]
lady, queen, wife of a khan (noun) [娘子 行]
accusative: marks the object (the (n) is Shiratori's)

sentences.l: Ladies-from, Jesüi Lady-(object), taking, went.
sentences.i: Of his ladies he took Lady Jesüi with him and set out.
sentences.n: Qatun-dāča is qatun “lady” + the plural -d + the ablative, “from among the ladies” (Ming 娘子 內, “among”); the long ā is as Shiratori prints it. Qatun-(n)i is the object (accusative, Ming 行), so Jesüi qatun is “Lady Jesüi” as the one taken. Abču “taking” is a converb of ab-, and odba “went” the main verb: “took and went”.

sentences.t: Žaγ̇ura übül Arbuqa-jin olon qulad-i abalaγ̇asu Čiṅgis Qaγan Žosotu-Boro-ji unužu büleġe.

morph.gloss: to hunt in a surround (verb; stem inferred from the Ming) [圍獵呵]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 (name) [太祖︀]
Josotu-Boro, a horse's name (name; meaning uncertain) [馬名行]
accusative: marks the object (-ji after a vowel)

sentences.l: Midway, winter, Arbuqa’s many wild-asses-(object) if-hunted, Chinggis Qaγan Žosotu-Boro-(object) riding, was.
sentences.i: On the way, in winter, when Chinggis Qahan hunted in a surround the many wild asses of Arbuqa, he was riding Josotu-Boro.
sentences.n: Žaγ̇ura is žaγ̇ur “midway” + the dative-locative -a (Ming 路間). Arbuqa-jin is a place name in the genitive, “of Arbuqa” (Ming 地名的). Qulad-i is qulan “wild ass” + the plural -d + the object ending; the Ming has 野馬, “wild horses”, but qulan is the wild ass. Abalaγ̇asu is abala- “hunt in a surround” + -γ̇asu “when”. Žosotu-Boro is the horse’s name (Ming 馬名); I do not know what it means. It carries the object ending -ji with unu- “mount, ride”, a verb that takes an object here. Unužu büleġe is converb + büleġe “was”, a continuing past: “was riding”.

sentences.t: Qulad daγ̇arižu ireġesü Žosotu-Boro ürġüžü Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)i morin-ača unaγ̇asu

morph.gloss: to pass by, go past (verb) [經過着]
to be frightened (verb; stem inferred from the Ming) [驚着]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 (name) [太祖︀]
accusative: marks the object (the (n) is Shiratori's)

sentences.l: Wild-asses passing-by, if-came, Žosotu-Boro being-frightened, Chinggis Qaγan-(object) horse-from if-fell,
sentences.i: when the wild asses came past and Josotu-Boro took fright, and Chinggis Qahan fell from his horse,
sentences.n: The conditional -γ̇asu/-ġesü (Ming 呵) sits on ireġesü “when (they) came” and unaγ̇asu “when (he) fell”; ürġüžü is a converb, “being frightened” (Ming 驚着). Qaγan-(n)i has the object ending (Ming 行) although una- “fall” is intransitive, which suggests a causative, “threw him”, or a looser use. The Ming gives only 倒了, “fell”, and I follow it. Morin-ača is “from the horse”.

sentences.t: marija-ban maši ebedčü Soγ̇oroqad baγ̇uba.

morph.gloss: to hurt, ache (verb; stem inferred from the Ming) [疼着]

sentences.l: Body-his-own greatly aching, So’oroqad camped.
sentences.i: his body aching badly, he camped at So’oroqad.
sentences.n: Marija-ban is marija “body” + the reflexive-possessive -ban, “his own body” (Ming 肌膚 自的行); the Ming glosses 肌膚 for marija. Ebedčü is ebed- “ache” (stem inferred from the Ming 疼) + the converb -čü. Soγ̇oroqad (Ming 地名) is a place; later, with the dative-locative, it is printed Soγ̇orqad-ta. Baγ̇uba “came down” is the camp verb, “camped”.

sentences.t: Tere süni qonoγ̇asu manaγar Jesüi Qatun ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Yesui, a woman's name (personal name) [(婦人)名]
lady, queen, wife of a khan (noun) [娘子]
converb of time: when, while -ing (front-vowel form)

sentences.l: That night, if-spent-the-night, tomorrow Jesüi Lady, when-saying:
sentences.i: When he had spent that night there, in the morning Lady Jesüi said:
sentences.n: Qonoγ̇asu is qono- “spend the night” + the conditional -γ̇asu (Ming 宿呵): “when (he) had lodged”. Manaγar is “tomorrow, the next morning”. Ügülerün is ügüle- “speak” + -rün “when saying”, the usual way a speech is introduced; the colon is Shiratori’s.

sentences.t: "Köġüd nojad keleleldüdkün.

morph.gloss: to speak, converse (kele “tongue” + verb-maker; stem read from the Ming) [共說話]

sentences.l: "Princes, officers, speak-together-you-all!
sentences.i: “Princes and officers, confer together.
sentences.n: Köġüd nojad is köġün “son” (here “prince”, Ming 大王每) and nojan “officer”, both in the plural -d. Keleleldüdkün is kelele- “speak” (kele “tongue” + a verb-maker, as in the published parts) + the reciprocal -ldü- + -dkün, a polite plural imperative (as in iredkün later), Ming 共說話 “talk together”. The quotation opens here.

sentences.t: Qaγan süni marija qalaγ̇un qonoba" keġebe.
sentences.l: Qaγan night body hot spent-the-night" said.
sentences.i: The Qahan passed the night with his body hot,” she said.
sentences.n: Marija qalaγ̇un is “body hot”, two words side by side with no verb (Ming 肌膚 熱); the Qahan, after the fall, has a fever (my reading of 熱 “hot”). Qonoba is the plain past, “spent the night”. The closing quotation mark is printed after it, and keġebe “said” follows.

sentences.t: Tende köġüd nojad quraγ̇asu Qoṅγotadai Tolun Čerbi duradγan ügülerün:

morph.gloss: to gather, assemble (verb; stem inferred from the Ming) [衆呵]
the Qongqotadai, a people (proper name) [種名]
Tolun, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
cherbi, an office or rank (meaning of the title not known) (noun) [(官名)]
converb of time: when, while -ing (front-vowel form)

sentences.l: There, princes officers if-assembled, Qongqotadai Tolun cherbi, when-recalling, when-saying:
sentences.i: When the princes and officers had gathered there, Tolun the cherbi of the Qongqotadai raised the matter and said:
sentences.n: Quraγ̇asu is a stem qura- “gather” (inferred from the Ming 衆) + the conditional -γ̇asu (Ming 呵). Qoṅγotadai is a people (Ming 種名) and Tolun a name; čerbi is a rank whose meaning is not known, as in earlier parts. Duradγan “mentioning” (Ming 提) is a converb in -n; with ügülerün the sense is “bringing it up, he said”.

sentences.t: "Taṅγ̇ud irgen nödügsen balaγasutan nunži nutuγtan bi.

morph.gloss: the Tangut, a people (people name; plural in -d) [種名]
to build, set up (verb; stem inferred from the Ming) [築了的]
past participle: that has been -ed (front-vowel form)
town, city (noun; the final n lost) [城 有的(每)]
unmoving, fixed (adjective; stem not clear) [不動的]
is, exists (verb; short form, perhaps of bü-) [有]

sentences.l: "Tangut people, built towns-having, unmoving camps-having are.
sentences.i: “The Tangut people have built towns and fixed camps.
sentences.n: Nödügsen is nödü- “build” (stem inferred from the Ming 築) + the participle -gsen, “that has been built”. Balaγasutan is balaγasun “town” + the possessive plural -tan (Ming 有的每), “those having towns”; nutuγtan is the same with nutuγ “camp”. Nunži (Ming 不動的 “unmoving”) is a word whose stem I cannot read. Bi (Ming 有) is “is, are”, a short form of the verb “to be”.

sentences.t: Nödügsen balaγasu-ban üġürčü ülü odqun.

morph.gloss: to build, set up (verb; stem inferred from the Ming) [築了的]
past participle: that has been -ed (front-vowel form)
town, city (noun; the final n lost) [城 自的行]
to carry, lift (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 擡) [擡着]

sentences.l: Built town-their-own carrying not will-go.
sentences.i: They will not go off carrying their built towns.
sentences.n: Balaγasu-ban is the town with the reflexive-possessive -ban, “their own town”. Üġürčü is a converb of a stem I infer from the Ming 擡, “lift, carry”. Ülü odqun is “not go”; the ending -qun is a participle or a hortative, I cannot tell which, so “will not go” is the plain reading.

sentences.t: Tede nunži nutug(i)-jan gežü ülü odqun tede.

morph.gloss: unmoving, fixed (adjective; stem not clear) [不動的]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (back-vowel form; the (i) is Shiratori's)
to cast aside, abandon (verb; per the Ming, possibly keġe- in an idiom, uncertain) [撇着]

sentences.l: Those, unmoving camp-their-own casting-aside, not will-go, those.
sentences.i: Nor will they go, leaving their fixed camps behind; they will not.
sentences.n: Gežü (Ming 撇着, “casting aside”) is a puzzle. It may be the verb keġe- “say” in an idiom, but I follow the Ming. Nutug(i)-jan is nutuγ “camp” + the reflexive -(i)jan, the (i) being Shiratori’s. The final tede “those” repeats the subject for emphasis; this reading is mine.

sentences.t: Bida ičužu Qaγan-(n)u maraγ̇a seriġüdüġesü basa žiči morilad-že bida"

morph.gloss: to withdraw, draw back (verb; stem inferred from the Ming) [退着]
genitive: of (back-vowel form; the (n) is Shiratori's)
body, flesh (noun; here spelled maraγ̇a) [肌膚]
to cool, grow cool (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 凉) [凉了呵]

sentences.l: We withdrawing, Qaγan’s body if-cooled, again then let-us-mount, we"
sentences.i: Let us draw back; and when the Qahan’s body has cooled, let us mount again then.”
sentences.n: Bida “we” (Ming 咱) is the inclusive pronoun, standing at the head of the clause and again as the last word, a bracketing. Ičužu is a converb of ič-/ičü- “withdraw” (stem inferred, Ming 退着); seriġüdüġesü is “if (it) cooled” (Ming 凉了呵), a stem I read from the Ming. Morilad-že is mori + -la- + -d + -že (Ming 上馬也者): “let us ride, indeed”, where I take -d as a plural mark. Žiči (Ming 郤) is “but, yet”; I read it as “then”. The closing quotation mark is printed after the last bida.

sentences.t: keġeġesü bürin köġüd nojad ene üge žöbšiježü Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)a öčiġešü Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün:

morph.gloss: to approve, agree to (verb; stem probably žöbšiye-) [道是着]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 (name) [太祖︀]
dative-locative: to (back-vowel form; the (n) is Shiratori's)
to say to a superior, to report (verb) [奏呵]
conditional converb: if, when (front-vowel form; printed -ġešü)
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 (name) [太祖︀]
converb of time: when, while -ing (front-vowel form)

sentences.l: If-said, all princes officers this word approving, Chinggis Qaγan-to if-reported, Chinggis Qaγan when-saying:
sentences.i: When he had said this, all the princes and officers approved the word and reported it to Chinggis Qahan; and Chinggis Qahan said:
sentences.n: Žöbšiježü is a converb of žöbšije- “agree, approve” (Ming 道是着). Öčiġešü, printed with š, is öči- “say to a superior” + the conditional, a reporting upward (Ming 奏呵). Chinggis Qahan then speaks in the next units; the message that follows, in his name, runs to aisai" in U25.

sentences.t: "Taṅγ̇ud irgen bidan-i žürüge jadažu qariba keġekün.

morph.gloss: the Tangut, a people (people name; plural in -d) [種名]
we, us (inclusive: you and I) (pronoun) [咱行]
to be unable, to lack (verb) [不能着]

sentences.l: "Tangut people, us-(object) heart being-unable returned they-will-say.
sentences.i: “The Tangut people will say of us that our hearts failed and we turned back.
sentences.n: Bidan-i is bida “we” with the stem extension -n and the object ending (Ming 咱行): they will say it of us. Žürüge jadažu is “heart” + the converb of jada- “be unable” (Ming 心 不能着), “the heart failing”; qariba “turned back”. Keġekün is keġe- “say” + -kün (Ming 說他的, “they will say”), an ending I cannot name exactly.

sentences.t: Bida elčin maqa iležü.

morph.gloss: who knows, perhaps; here 'first, for the time' (particle) [且]
to send (verb; Ming 敎去着, causing to go) [敎去着]

sentences.l: We envoy perhaps sending.
sentences.i: Let us first send an envoy.
sentences.n: Maqa (Ming 且, “for the time being”) is usually “perhaps”; here the Ming reads “first”. Iležü is a converb of ile- “send” (Ming 敎去着, “causing to go”) closing the clause where a finite verb would be expected.

sentences.t: elčin-i mün ene Soγ̇orqad-ta sobilažu üge an-u uqažu ičuγ̇asu bolu-že" keġežü

words.reading: 搠斡舌兒中合惕-塔 Soγ̇orqad-ta

morph.gloss: So'oroqad, a place (place name; the same as Soγ̇oroqad) [地(名)行]
to test, try out (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 試) [試着]
their (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
to understand, perceive, find out (verb) [省着]
to withdraw, retreat (verb; stem inferred) [退呵]
conditional: linking vowel u, then -γ̇asu, if, when

sentences.l: Envoy-(object) just this So’oroqad-in testing, word their understanding, if-withdrawing, let-it-be" saying,
sentences.i: Let us test them by an envoy here at So’oroqad; and when we have understood their answer, if we then withdraw, let it be so,” he said,
sentences.n: A doubtful unit. Elčin-i has the object ending (Ming 行), so literally “testing the envoy”; I read it as “by means of the envoy”. Sobilažu (Ming 試着) is a stem sobila- “test”; üge an-u uqažu is “word their finding out” with an-u “their” placed after its noun. Ičuγ̇asu bolu-že is “if (we) withdraw, so be it” (Ming 退呵 中 也者). The closing quotation mark follows bolu-že. Keġežü “saying” closes the speech.

sentences.t: tende elčin-e daγ̇u bariγ̇ulužu ilerün:

morph.gloss: converb of time: when, while -ing (front-vowel form)

sentences.l: There envoy-to word having-it-carried, when-sending:
sentences.i: and there he had the envoy carry a word, and as he sent him said:
sentences.n: Daγ̇u “voice, word, message” (Ming 把, “take”) is the thing carried; bariγ̇ulužu is bari- “hold” + the causative -γ̇ul- + the converb -užu (Ming 把話着, “making hold the word”). Ilerün “when sending” is ile- + -rün. The message that follows is Chinggis’s to the Tangut ruler.

sentences.t: "Nidoni Burqan či ügülerün;

morph.gloss: Burqan, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
converb of time: when, while -ing (front-vowel form)

sentences.l: "Last-year, Burqan, you when-speaking;
sentences.i: “Last year, Burqan, when you spoke,
sentences.n: Nidoni is “last year”. Burqan here is the Tangut ruler’s name (Ming 人名), not the mountain. Či is “you”. Ügülerün “when speaking” with the semicolon: the thing he said comes next.

sentences.t: ba Taṅγ̇ud irgen baraγ̇un γar čin-u bolsu keġelüġe.

morph.gloss: we (first-person plural pronoun; Ming 俺) [俺]
the Tangut, a people (people name; plural in -d) [種名]
you, thou (pronoun; oblique stem čin-) [你的]
genitive: of, your (set after the stem čin-)
optative: let me / let us be

sentences.l: We Tangut people right hand your let-be, said-had.
sentences.i: ‘Let us, the Tangut people, be your right hand,’ you said.
sentences.n: Ba (Ming 俺) is “we”, the exclusive form against bida. Baraγ̇un γar is “right hand” (Ming 右 手); čin-u is či “you” on its oblique stem + the genitive, “your”, set after the noun it owns. Bolsu is bol- “be” + the optative -su, “let us be” (Ming 做我), and keġelüġe is keġe- + -lüġe, “had said”. The inner quotation has no marks printed; I supply single quotes in `i`.

sentences.t: Čima-da tein keġegdežü Sartaγ̇ul irgen-e eje-dür(i)-jen ese oroγdažu morilasu keġen γujužu ileġesü

morph.gloss: you, thou (pronoun; oblique stem čima-) [你 行]
the Sartaul, a people (people name) [囘囘]
people, the common folk (noun) [百姓 行]
counsel, consulting (noun; stem unknown, read from the Ming 商量) [商量 裏自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (front-vowel form; the (i) is Shiratori's)
not (negates a past action; ülü negates present or future) (negative particle) [不曾]

sentences.l: You-to thus being-told, Sartaul people-to in-counsel-own not being-entered, let-me-mount saying, asking, if-sent,
sentences.i: Having been told so by you, and I not yet drawn into the counsel of the Sartaul people, when I said ‘Let me ride’ and sent to ask you,
sentences.n: A doubtful unit. Čima-da is či “you” on the stem čima- + the dative-locative; tein keġegdežü is “thus being told” (Ming 被說着), with keġe- made passive, so “told by you”. Eje-dür(i)-jen is eje “counsel” (Ming 商量) + the dative-locative + the reflexive -(i)jen, “in one’s own counsel”; ese oroγdažu is “not having been entered” (oro- + the passive -γda-). Whose counsel, and who was or was not brought into it, I cannot settle: the reflexive points to the speaker, the Ming 被入着 to someone else. Morilasu is “let me ride”, γujužu “asking for” and ileġesü “if (I) sent”.

sentences.t: či Burqan üge-dür(i)-jen ülü kürün čerig ba ülü ögün üge-ġer daγ̇arižu irežü büleġe.

morph.gloss: Burqan, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
word, speech (noun) [言語 裏自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (front-vowel form; the (i) is Shiratori's)
instrumental: with, by means of (front-vowel form)
to taunt, mock (verb; Ming 譏諷; compare daγ̇ari- 'pass by') [譏諷着]

sentences.l: You Burqan word-in-own not arriving, army also not giving, with-words mocking coming, were.
sentences.i: you, Burqan, did not keep to your own word and gave no army either, but came mocking with words.
sentences.n: Üge-dür(i)-jen is üge “word” + the dative-locative + the reflexive -(i)jen, and ülü kürün (Ming 不 到, “not reaching”) is “not arriving at one’s own word”, that is, not making good one’s word. Čerig ba ülü ögün is “army also not giving” (ba after a noun, “also”). Üge-ġer is “by words” (the instrumental, Ming 言語 敎); daγ̇arižu is a form of daγ̇ari- “mock” (Ming 譏諷着), which elsewhere means “pass by”. Irežü büleġe is “came”, a continuing past.

sentences.t: Öġere žoriγsan-dur qoina olulčasu keġen

words.reading: 勺舌里黑三-突︀舌兒 žoriγsan-dur

morph.gloss: to aim at, set out for (verb) [扯了的 裏]
after, behind, later (postposition or adverb) [在後]

sentences.l: Other aimed-at-in, later let-me-settle, saying,
sentences.i: Thinking, ‘I have another aim; afterwards let me settle with you,’
sentences.n: Another doubtful unit. Öġere is “other, apart” (Ming 𠮠, 別). Žoriγsan-dur is žori- “aim at” + the participle -γsan + the dative-locative (Ming 扯了的 裏), “in what was aimed at”. Qoina is “afterwards”. Olulčasu is ol- “find, get” + a reciprocal -lča- + the optative -su, Ming 折證我, “let me have it out”; I take it as “settle accounts”. The sentence’s first thought is therefore a thought inside Chinggis’s speech; no marks are printed, so I add single quotes in `i`.

sentences.t: Sartaγ̇ul irgen-dür morilažu müṅke teṅgeri-de igeġegdežü Sartaγ̇ul irgen-i žüg-tür oroγ̇ulžu

morph.gloss: the Sartaul, a people (people name) [囘囘]
people, the common folk (noun) [百姓 行]
Heaven, the sky as a power (noun) [天 行]
to protect, help (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 護助) [被護助着]
the Sartaul, a people (people name) [囘囘]
people, the common folk (noun) [百姓 行]
direction, side (noun; Ming 正 'right, proper') [正行]
dative-locative: at, in, to (front-vowel form, after a consonant)

sentences.l: Sartaul people-to mounting, Eternal Heaven-by being-helped, Sartaul people-(object) direction-in having-made-enter,
sentences.i: I rode against the Sartaul people, was helped by Eternal Heaven, and brought the Sartaul people into line,
sentences.n: Sartaγ̇ul is the Sartaul (the Ming 囘囘, “Muslims”). Müṅke teṅgeri-de is “Eternal Heaven” + the dative-locative, naming the doer of the passive igeġegdežü “being helped” (igeġe- “protect, help” + -gde- + -žü, Ming 被護助着). Žüg-tür oroγ̇ulžu is žüg “direction” + the dative-locative + oro- “enter” in the causative (Ming 正行 敎入着, “making enter the right way”); “brought into line” is my rendering of that.

sentences.t: edöġe Burqan-dur üge olulčasu keġen aisai"

words.reading: 不舌兒中罕-突︀舌兒 Burqan-dur

morph.gloss: Burqan, a man's name (personal name) [人名 行]
ending of the present: is coming (uncertain)

sentences.l: Now Burqan-to word let-me-settle, saying, is-coming"
sentences.i: and now I am coming, saying ‘Let me settle with Burqan over his word.’”
sentences.n: Burqan-dur is a personal name + the dative-locative, “to Burqan”, which is odd in a speech addressed to him; but the Ming has 人名 行 and I follow it. Aisai is ai- “come” (stem uncertain) + -sai, a present ending (Ming 來也), “is coming”. The closing double quotation mark is printed here, ending the whole message begun at Nidoni.

sentences.t: keġežü ileġesü Burqan ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Burqan, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
converb of time: when, while -ing (front-vowel form)

sentences.l: Saying, if-sent, Burqan when-saying:
sentences.i: Having said that, when the envoy had gone Burqan said:
sentences.n: Keġežü ileġesü is “saying, if (he) sent / went” (Ming 說着 去呵). The one who goes is the envoy, and whose act it is is not stated; I read it as “when the envoy had gone”. Burqan then answers.

sentences.t: "Daγ̇ariqu üge bi ese ügülelüġe"

morph.gloss: to taunt, mock (verb; Ming 譏諷) [譏諷的]
not (negates a past action; ülü negates present or future) (negative particle) [不曾]

sentences.l: "Mocking word I not spoken-had"
sentences.i: “I did not speak a mocking word,”
sentences.n: Daγ̇ariqu is the participle of daγ̇ari- “mock” (Ming 譏諷的), “mocking”. Ese ügülelüġe is ese “not” (of a past act) + ügüle- “say” + -lüġe “had said” (Ming 說來).

sentences.t: keġežüġüi Ašaγambu ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Asha Gambu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
converb of time: when, while -ing (front-vowel form)

sentences.l: said, Asha Gambu when-saying:
sentences.i: he said. Asha Gambu said:
sentences.n: Keġežüġüi is keġe- “say” + the past -žüġüi, the front-vowel form of -žuγ̇ui, the same ending as in later units. Ašaγambu is a man’s name, Asha Gambu (Ming 人名), speaking in turn.

sentences.t: "Daγ̇ariqu üges bi ügülelüġe.

morph.gloss: to taunt, mock (verb; Ming 譏諷) [譏諷的]

sentences.l: "Mocking words I spoken-had.
sentences.i: “I did say mocking words.
sentences.n: The same daγ̇ariqu again, but now üges, plural “words” (Ming 言語每), where Burqan had the singular; whether the plural is meant to stress the point I cannot say. Bi ügülelüġe is “I had said”, with no ese, so the opposite of Burqan’s denial. Asha Gambu is taking the word on himself.

sentences.t: Edöġe ber böġesü ta Monγol qadqulduγ̇a surču qadquldusu keġeġesü

words.reading: 中合惕中忽勒都︀阿 qadqulduγ̇a

morph.gloss: to learn, be practised (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 慣) [慣着]

words.reading: 中合惕中忽勒都︀速 qadquldusu

sentences.l: Now even if-it-is, you Mongols fighting practised, let-us-fight if-say,
sentences.i: Even now, if you Mongols, practised in fighting, say ‘Let us fight,’
sentences.n: Böġesü is bü- “be” + the conditional, “if it is so” (Ming 有呵). Qadqulduγ̇a is qadqu- “strike, fight” + the reciprocal -ldu- + -γ̇a, an ending whose force I cannot name; surču is a converb of a stem sur- “learn, be practised” (Ming 慣着). Qadquldusu is “let us fight” (optative -su, Ming 斷殺我) and keġeġesü “if (you) say”. The quotation inside the speech has no marks printed; I supply single quotes in `i`.

sentences.t: bi bürün Alašai nutuγtu terme gertü temeġen ačiγ̇atu bijü.

morph.gloss: Alashai (the Helan mountains), a mountain (mountain name) [賀蘭山名]

sentences.l: I as-for, Alashai camp-having, spread-tent house-having, camel load-having, am.
sentences.i: I, for my part, have my camp at Alashai, with spread tents and loaded camels.
sentences.n: Bi bürün is “I, as for me” (bürün, Ming 呵, marks the topic). Alašai is a mountain name (Ming 賀蘭山), the Helan range. Nutuγtu is nutuγ + -tu “having a camp”; terme gertü is terme “spread tent” + ger “house” + -tü; temeġen ačiγ̇atu is “camels having loads”, ačiγ̇a “load” + -tu. The -tu/-tü/-tai/-tei possessive chain, each noun “having” something, is the pattern to notice.

sentences.t: Alašai žorižü na-dur iredkün.

morph.gloss: Alashai (the Helan mountains), a mountain (mountain name) [山名]
to aim at, set out for (verb) [指着]
I (first-person singular pronoun; oblique stem na-) [我行]

sentences.l: Alashai aiming, me-to come-you-all.
sentences.i: Aim for Alashai and come to me.
sentences.n: Žorižü is a converb of žori- “aim at” (Ming 指着), na-dur is bi “I” on the stem na- + the dative-locative, “to me”; iredkün is ire- “come” + the polite plural imperative -dkün, as in keleleldüdkün in U7.

sentences.t: Tende qadqulduja.

words.reading: 中合惕中忽勒都︀牙 qadqulduja

sentences.l: There let-us-fight.
sentences.i: There let us fight.
sentences.n: Qadquldu- is “fight one another” with the hortative -ja, “let us” (Ming 厮殺咱).

sentences.t: Altan müṅgün aγ̇urasun tabar keregtü böġesü Ariγaja, Erižeġü-ji žoridqun" keġežü iležüġüi.

morph.gloss: length of cloth (noun; stem as printed, uncertain) [段疋]
Ningxia, a Chinese city (place name; the Ming 甯夏) [甯夏]
Xiliang, a Chinese city (place name; the Ming 西涼) [西涼行]
accusative: marks the object (-ji after a vowel)
to aim at, set out for (verb) [指着您]

sentences.l: Gold silver cloth goods needing if-it-be, Ningxia, Xiliang-(object) aim-you-all" saying, he-sent.
sentences.i: If you need gold, silver, silks and goods, aim for Ningxia and Xiliang,” he said, and sent word.
sentences.n: Keregtü is kereg “need” + -tü, “having need”, + böġesü “if it be”: “if you need”. Aγ̇urasun (Ming 段疋, “bolts of silk”) is a noun I cannot confirm from the stem alone. Ariγaja (Ming 甯夏) and Erižeġü (Ming 西涼) are two places of the Tangut land; I give them as Ningxia and Xiliang, the Chinese names the Ming writes. The object ending -ji stands after the last name and covers both. Žoridqun is a plural imperative of žori-, and iležüġüi is ile- “send” + the past -žüġüi (Ming 敎去了), “he sent (it)”. The closing quotation mark is printed after žoridqun.

sentences.t: Ene üge-ji Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)a kürgeġesü Čiṅgis Qaγan marija qalaγ̇un arün ügülerün:

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (-ji after a vowel)
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 (name) [太祖︀]
dative-locative: to (back-vowel form; the (n) is Shiratori's)
to bring to, deliver (verb; kür- made causative, uncertain) [送到呵]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 (name) [太祖︀]
converb of time: when, while -ing (front-vowel form)

sentences.l: This word-(object) Chinggis Qaγan-to if-delivered, Chinggis Qaγan body hot while-being, when-saying:
sentences.i: When this word was brought to Chinggis Qahan, Chinggis Qahan, his body still hot, said:
sentences.n: Üge-ji has the object ending, “the word” as what is delivered; kürgeġesü is kürge- “bring to” (kür- “reach” made causative, uncertain) + the conditional. Arün is a- “be” + -rün, “being” (Ming 有時); marija qalaγ̇un is the fever of the earlier unit. Chinggis’s speech follows after the colon.

sentences.t: "Že! Teli eimü jeke üge üġüleġülžü ker ičuγdaqui.

morph.gloss: particle: enough, so be it (the Ming 罷) [罷]
to speak (a spelling of ügüle-) (verb) [敎說着]
to withdraw, draw back (verb; stem inferred from the Ming) [可退有]

sentences.l: "Enough! That matter such great word having-made-to-speak, how withdrawn-is?
sentences.i: “Enough! When they have made so great a speech, how can we draw back?
sentences.n: Že (Ming 罷) here is “enough, very well”. Teli is read from the Ming as “that matter”, and I am not sure of the word. Eimü jeke üge is “such a great word”; üġüleġülžü is üġüle- “speak” + the causative -ġül- + the converb -žü (Ming 敎說着), “having made (them) speak”. Ker is “how”; ičuγdaqui is ičü- “withdraw” + the passive -γda- + a participle -qui, “can (it) be withdrawn”.

sentences.t: Ükürün jeke üge-dür šiqan jabuja"

morph.gloss: converb of time: when dying (after a vowel stem)
to lean against, keep close to (verb; stem inferred from the Ming) [靠着]

sentences.l: Dying great word-in leaning let-us-go"
sentences.i: If we are to die, let us go on leaning on a great word.”
sentences.n: Ükürün is ükü- “die” + the converb of time -rün, “when dying” (Ming 死時). Üge-dür is “in the word” + the dative-locative; šiqan is the converb of šiqa- “lean against” (stem inferred, Ming 靠着). Jabuja is “let us go”. The closing quotation mark is printed after it.

sentences.t: keġežü müṅke teṅgeri či mede" keġen

morph.gloss: Heaven, the sky as a power (noun) [天]

sentences.l: saying, Eternal Heaven you know" saying,
sentences.i: Having said this, and saying “Eternal Heaven, you know it,”
sentences.n: Mede is the bare stem of mede- “know”, taken as a bare statement or an imperative (the Ming 知 does not decide); či is “you”. The closing mark is printed after mede with no opening mark before müṅke; I supply the opening in `i` in double quotes: the first speech closed after jabuja, so this is a second quotation, not an inner one. Keġen “saying” closes it.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan Alašai žorižü kürčü Ašaγambu-luγ̇a qadquldužu Ašaγambu-ji daružu

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 (name) [太祖︀]
Alashai (the Helan mountains), a mountain (mountain name) [山名]
to aim at, set out for (verb) [指着]
Asha Gambu, a man's name (personal name) [人名 一同]

words.reading: 中合惕中忽勒都︀周 qadquldužu

morph.gloss: Asha Gambu, a man's name (personal name) [人名行]
accusative: marks the object (-ji after a vowel)

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan Alashai aiming, arriving, Asha Gambu-with fighting, Asha Gambu-(object) overcoming,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan made for Alashai, arrived, fought Asha Gambu and overcame him,
sentences.n: Ašaγambu-luγ̇a is the comitative, “with Asha Gambu” (Ming 一同); qadquldužu is qadqul- “fight” + -du- + the converb, “fighting each other”. Ašaγambu-ji is the object of daružu “overcoming” (daru- “press down, overcome”, Ming 勝着). These converbs lead the action up to abču in the next unit.

sentences.t: Alašai deġere qorγolaγ̇ulžu Ašaγambu-ji abču

morph.gloss: Alashai (the Helan mountains), a mountain (mountain name) [山名]

words.reading: 中豁舌兒中豁剌兀勒周 qorγolaγ̇ulžu

glyphs.s: 中豁舌兒中豁剌兀勒周

morph.gloss: stockade, enclosure (noun; Ming 寨) [寨把着]
Asha Gambu, a man's name (personal name) [人名行]
accusative: marks the object (-ji after a vowel)

sentences.l: Alashai on, having-made-stockade, Asha Gambu-(object) taking,
sentences.i: had a stockade made on Alashai, and took Asha Gambu,
sentences.n: Qorγolaγ̇ulžu is qorγo “stockade” + -la- “make into” + the causative -γ̇ul- + the converb -žu (Ming 寨把着, “holding a stockade”), as in the published qorγolaγsan. Who held the stockade, and whether it was set up or besieged, I cannot tell; “had a stockade made” follows the form, and the sense may be a siege. Deġere is “on, above”. Abču “taking” leads on to the sack in the next unit.

sentences.t: terme gertü temeġen ačiγ̇atu irgen-i in-ü hunesü-ġer keistele talaγ̇ulba.

morph.gloss: people, the common folk (noun) [百姓 行]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
instrumental: with, by means of (front-vowel form)
to scrape (verb; stem as in the published keisgen 'scraped off') [般直到]

sentences.l: Spread-tent house-having, camel load-having people-(object) his, ash-with scraping-until, had-plundered.
sentences.i: and had his people of the spread tents and the loaded camels plundered, until nothing was left, not even ash.
sentences.n: Terme gertü temeġen ačiγ̇atu irgen-i in-ü is the same four-word possessive string as in U31, now “the people, with spread tents and loaded camels, his”; in-ü “his” is set after the noun. Hunesü-ġer keistele is hünesü “ash, dust” + the instrumental + keis- “scrape” (stem as in the published keisgen, Ming 刮 there) + -tele “until”, with the Ming 灰飛 般 直到, “till even the ashes were blown away”; I read it as an idiom for total destruction. Talaγ̇ulba is tala- “plunder” + the causative -γ̇ul- + -ba, “had (them) plundered”.

sentences.t: Erekün omoγun erebin said Taṅγ̇udud-i kidužu

morph.gloss: daring, bold (adjective; read here as ere 'man' with -kün, 'brave one') [勇]
quarrelsome, ready to fight others (adjective) [猛的]
the Tangut, a people (people name) [種名每行]
to cut off, destroy utterly, slaughter (verb) [殺︀着]

sentences.l: Brave, fierce, men, good (ones) Tanguts-(object) slaughtering,
sentences.i: “Having slaughtered the brave and fierce, the men and the best of the Tanguts,
sentences.n: Erekün is read as ere “man” + -kün, “brave one” (Ming 勇, with 敢望 elsewhere), and omoγun (Ming 與人相鬭) as “quarrelsome, ready to fight”; erebin (Ming 男子) is “men” (an ending I cannot parse), and said, from sain “good” + the plural -d, is “the good ones” (Ming 好每). Taṅγ̇udud-i is Taṅγ̇ud + the plural -ud + the object ending (Ming 種名每行). Kidužu is kidu- “cut off, slaughter” (Ming 殺着). The decree’s opening quotation mark is not printed; I supply it in `i`.

sentences.t: eimün teimün Taṅγ̇udud-i čeriġüd küġün-e bariγsaγ̇ar oluγsaγ̇ar abudqun" keġen žarliγ bolba.

morph.gloss: such, of this kind (adjective or pronoun) [這般]
the Tangut, a people (people name) [種名每行]

words.reading: 把舌里黑撒阿舌兒 bariγsaγ̇ar

morph.gloss: instrumental: with, by means of, according to (back-vowel form)
instrumental: with, by means of, according to (back-vowel form)

sentences.l: Such, such Tanguts, soldiers each-man-to, according-to-seized, according-to-got, take-you-all" saying, decree made.
sentences.i: take the Tanguts of every kind, you soldiers, each of you according to what you have seized and what you have got,” he said, and issued a decree.
sentences.n: Eimün teimün is “such and such, of this kind and that” (Ming 這般 那般), so “of every kind”. Čeriġüd is čerig “soldier” + a linking vowel + the plural -d; küġün-e is küġün “person” (not köġün “son”) + the dative, “to a man” (Ming 人行), “each”. Bariγsaγ̇ar and oluγsaγ̇ar are bari- “seize” and ol- “get” + the participle -γsan + the instrumental -γ̇ar, “according to what is seized / got” (Ming 依着). Abudqun is “take (all of you)”; I read čeriġüd as addressed, since abudqun is second person. Keġen žarliγ bolba is the formula: “saying, he issued a decree”. The closing quotation mark is printed after abudqun.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan Časutu deġere žusažu

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 (name) [太祖︀]
Chasutu, 'Snow Mountain' (mountain name; Ming 雪山名) [雪山名]

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan Chasutu on summer-spending,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan spent the summer on Chasutu,
sentences.n: Časutu (Ming 雪山名, “snow mountain”) is a mountain name. Žusažu is žun “summer” + the verb-maker -sa- + the converb -žu, “summering” (Ming 住夏着), the counterpart of übülžežü in U0.

sentences.t: Ašaγambu-luγ̇a aγ̇ulalaγsad daižiγsad terme gerten temeġen ačiγ̇ata Taṅγ̇udud-i

morph.gloss: Asha Gambu, a man's name (personal name) [人名 一同]
mountain (noun; Ming 山) [山上了的每]
verb-maker: to go up a mountain (uncertain)
past participle: that has -ed (back-vowel form; the final n is lost before -d)
to rebel, make enemy (verb; stem read from the Ming 反, uncertain) [反了的每]
past participle: that has -ed (back-vowel form; the final n is lost before -d)
the Tangut, a people (people name) [種名(每)行]

sentences.l: Asha Gambu-with mountain-going-ones, rebelling-ones, spread-tent house-having, camel load-having Tanguts-(object),
sentences.i: and, as for the Tanguts who had taken to the mountain with Asha Gambu and rebelled, those of the spread tents and the loaded camels,
sentences.n: Aγ̇ulalaγsad (Ming 山上了的每) is aγ̇ula “mountain” + -la- + the participle -γsan + the plural -d, “those who went up the mountain”; daižiγsad (Ming 反了的每) “those who rebelled”, a stem I cannot parse further. Gerten and ačiγ̇ata are the possessive plural -ten and -ta, “those having houses, those having loads”, the plural of the -tü/-tu used in U31. Taṅγ̇udud-i is the object of talaγ̇ulba at the end of the sentence.

sentences.t: čeriġüd iležü onoγsaγ̇ar ülidtele talaγ̇ulba.

morph.gloss: to reckon, plan (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 算計) [算計了的依着]
instrumental: with, by means of, according to (back-vowel form)
to destroy utterly (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 盡絕) [直盡絕]

sentences.l: soldiers sending, according-to-reckoned, until-destroyed, had-plundered.
sentences.i: he sent soldiers and, as he had reckoned, had them plundered until all were destroyed.
sentences.n: Čeriġüd is čerig “soldier” + a linking vowel + -d; iležü “sending” (Ming 敎去着). Onoγsaγ̇ar is ono- “reckon, plan” (stem inferred, Ming 算計了的) + -γsan + -γ̇ar, “according to what was reckoned”; I read it as “as planned”. Ülidtele is a stem ülid- “destroy utterly” + -tele “until” (Ming 直盡絕); talaγ̇ulba as in U41, “had (them) plundered”, so the soldiers are his instrument.

sentences.t: Tendēče Boγ̇orču, Muqali qojar-a sojurγarun:

morph.gloss: ablative: from (front-vowel form; long vowel as printed)
Bo'orchu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Muqali, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

words.reading: 莎余舌兒中合舌侖 sojurγarun

morph.gloss: to show favour, bestow grace (verb) [恩賜時]

sentences.l: There-from Bo’orchu, Muqali two-to, when-showing-favour:
sentences.i: Then, showing favour to the two, Bo’orchu and Muqali, he said:
sentences.n: Tendēče is tende “there” + the ablative -ēče (long vowel as printed, Ming 自那裏). Qojar-a is qojar “two” + the dative, “to the two” (Ming 兩箇行). Sojurγarun is sojurγa- “show favour” + the converb of time -run, “when showing favour” (Ming 恩賜時). The speech follows.

sentences.t: "Küčün-e medetele abtuγai" keġen žarliγ bolba.

morph.gloss: strength, power (noun; stem küčün- before a case ending) [氣力行]
dative-locative: to, with, according to (front-vowel form)

sentences.l: "Strength-to until-managed let-him-take" saying, decree made.
sentences.i: “Let them take as much as their strength can manage,” he said, and issued a decree.
sentences.n: Küčün-e is küčü “strength” (küčün- before an ending) + the dative-locative, “to (their) strength”; medetele is mede- “know, manage” + -tele “until”, Ming 敎儘着, “to the full”. Abtuγai is ab- “take” + the third-person optative -tuγai, “let (them) take”. The opening quotation mark is printed at Küčün-e.

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolurun:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 (name) [太祖︀]
converb of time: when -ing (linking vowel, then -run)

sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan decree when-making:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan issued a decree:
sentences.n: Žarliγ bolurun is “when (he) made a decree”, a regular formula for a ruler’s order, introducing the speech.

sentences.t: "Boγ̇orču Muqali qojar-a sojurγal ögürün:

morph.gloss: Bo'orchu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Muqali, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
converb of time: when -ing (front-vowel form; linking vowel ü, then -rün)

sentences.l: "Bo’orchu Muqali two-to favour when-giving:
sentences.i: “When I give favour to the two of you, Bo’orchu and Muqali:
sentences.n: Sojurγal is “favour, bounty” (Ming 恩賜), ögürün is ög- “give” + -ürün “when giving” (Ming 與時). The colon, and the opening quotation mark before Kitad in the next unit, are Shiratori’s.

sentences.t: "Kitad irgen-eče ese ögüleġe keġen

morph.gloss: the Khitans, a people; here the Jin state and its people (people name) [契丹]
not (negates a past action; ülü negates present or future) (negative particle) [不曾]
past narrative: gave, had given (linking vowel, then -leġe)

sentences.l: "Kitad people-from not given-had saying,
sentences.i: ‘I have not yet given you anything from the Kitad people,’ thinking,
sentences.n: Kitad (Ming 契丹) is here the Jin state and its people. Irgen-eče is “from the people” (ablative; Ming 百姓處). Ese ögüleġe is ese “not” + ög- “give” + -üleġe, “had not given” (Ming 不曾 與來); keġen “saying” makes it a thought. Shiratori prints a second opening quotation mark at Kitad and no closing mark for it, so this is an inner quotation within the decree; I put it in single quotes in `i`.

sentences.t: Kitad irgen-ü Žüin-i ta qojar sačaγ̇u qubijaldužu abudqun.

morph.gloss: the Khitans, a people; here the Jin state and its people (people name) [契丹]
people, the common folk (noun) [百姓 的]
the Jüin, a people (proper name) [種名行]

sentences.l: Kitad people’s Jüin-(object), you two equally, sharing-among-yourselves, take-you-all.
sentences.i: Take the Jüin of the Kitad people, you two, sharing them out equally.
sentences.n: Irgen-ü is the genitive after n, “of the people”; Žüin-i is the Jüin (a people, Ming 種名) + the object ending. Sačaγ̇u is “alike, equally” (Ming 齊等). Qubijaldužu is qubi “share” + -ja- (a verb-maker I guess from the Ming) + the reciprocal -ldu- + the converb -žu (Ming 共分着). Abudqun is “take, all of you” as in U43.

sentences.t: Said köġüd-i an-u šibaγ̇u-ban bariγ̇ulužu daγaγ̇ulžu jabudqun.

morph.gloss: their (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
hawk, bird of prey (noun) [鷹 自的行]

sentences.l: Good-ones sons-(object) their hawk-own having-them-carry, having-them-follow, go-you-all.
sentences.i: As you go, have the sons of the good men carry their hawks and follow you.
sentences.n: Said is sain “good” + the plural -d, “the good ones” (Ming 好每). Köġüd-i is the plural of köġün “son” + the object ending, since the sons are the ones made to act; an-u “their”, after its noun. Šibaγ̇u-ban is the hawk with -ban “own”. Bariγ̇ulužu and daγaγ̇ulžu are causative converbs, “making hold” and “making follow” (Ming 敎拿着, 敎隨着); jabudqun is “go, all of you”, with the whole polite plural ending -dqun, as in abudqun.

sentences.t: Said ökid-i an-u ösgežü emes(i)-jen qormai žasaγ̇uludqun.

morph.gloss: their (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
to grow, bring up (verb; stem inferred) [敎長着]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (front-vowel form; the (i) is Shiratori's)
to put in order, arrange (verb) [敎整治您]

sentences.l: Good-ones daughters-(object) their having-brought-up, wives-own skirt-hem have-them-arrange.
sentences.i: Bring up the daughters of the good men, and have them tend the skirts of your wives.
sentences.n: Ökid-i is ökin “girl” + the plural -d + the object ending. Ösgežü is a converb of ösge- “bring up” (stem inferred, Ming 敎長着). Emes(i)-jen is emesi “wife” + the reflexive -(i)jen, “your own wives” (Ming 妻 自的行); qormai (here Ming 衣襟, the front of a robe; elsewhere 裙 “skirt”) is “skirt, hem”. Žasaγ̇uludqun is žasa- “put in order” + the causative + the plural imperative, “have (them) set in order”; I take the sense to be that the girls become the wives’ maids.

sentences.t: Kitad irgen-ü Altan Qān-(n)u itegelten inaγ̇ud

morph.gloss: the Khitans, a people; here the Jin state and its people (people name) [契丹]
people, the common folk (noun) [百姓 的]
gold (noun); in Altan Qān, the title of the Jin emperor [金]
genitive: of (back-vowel form; the (n) is Shiratori's)
possessive plural: those having (read as a variant of -tü; uncertain)
trusted one, favourite (noun; read from the Ming 寵信的) [寵信的每]

sentences.l: Kitad people’s, Altan Qān’s relied-on, favoured-ones,
sentences.i: Those whom Altan Qan relied on and favoured among the Kitad people,
sentences.n: Itegelten is itegel “reliance, trust” + the possessive plural -ten, “those having reliance” (Ming 倚仗的每); inaγ̇ud is inaγ “favourite” + the plural -ud (Ming 寵信的每). Qān-(n)u is the genitive, “of the Qan”, with Altan the title of the Jin emperor (Ming 金). Qān is the short form beside Qaγan, as house usage has it.

sentences.t: Moṅγol-un ebüges ečiges-i baraγsan Qara-Kitad, Žüin irgen ažuγ̇ui-že.

morph.gloss: to be finished, ruined (here transitive: to ruin) (verb) [廢了的]
the Qara-Kitad, 'Black Khitans', a people (name) [種名]
the Jüin, a people (proper name) [(種名)]

sentences.l: Mongols’ forefathers fathers-(object) ruined, Qara-Kitad, Jüin people were.
sentences.i: who had ruined the forefathers and fathers of the Mongols, were the Qara-Kitad, the Jüin people.
sentences.n: Ebüges ečiges-i are ebüge “forefather” and ečige “father” in the plural -s, the second with the object ending, “ruining the forefathers (and) fathers”; baraγsan is bara- “be ruined” used transitively + the participle -γsan (Ming 廢了的). Qara-Kitad (Ming 種名) and Žüin irgen name who they were; ažuγ̇ui-že is a- “be” + the past -žuγ̇ui + the particle -že (Ming 有來 也者), “were, indeed”.

sentences.t: Edöġe min-u itegelten inaγ̇ud Boγ̇orču, Muqali ta qojar bijü-že" keġen žarliγ bolba.

morph.gloss: I (first-person singular pronoun; oblique stem min-) [我的]
genitive: of, my (set after its noun)
possessive plural: those having (read as a variant of -tü; uncertain)
trusted one, favourite (noun; read from the Ming 寵信的) [寵信的每]
Bo'orchu, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
Muqali, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

sentences.l: Now my relied-on, favoured-ones, Bo’orchu, Muqali, you two are" saying, decree made.
sentences.i: Now my trusted and favoured ones are the two of you, Bo’orchu and Muqali,” he said, and issued a decree.
sentences.n: Min-u is bi “I” on the stem min- + the genitive set after its noun (Ming 我的); itegelten inaγ̇ud as in U55, now with “my”. Bijü-že is “are, indeed”, bijü being the present of “to be” + the particle -že (Ming 有 也者). The closing quotation mark is printed after bijü-že, and keġen žarliγ bolba ends the decree as at the end of U43.
